title: Card support tools' data
description: One item of the tools' data table, as a gold export writes it and the tools read it (ADR-0004, Stores; ADR-0006, Gold). The export holds these items in DynamoDB JSON; this schema describes them as plain JSON, numbers included. Every customer's items share its partition, so a tool reads one customer's records only. Transactions are read through the by_card index, which projects every attribute but is_fraud, so the read tools never hold it; file_handoff reads is_fraud from the transaction's own item (POL-40). Gold holds no full card number, identity document, or contact field (POL-11, SEC-03).

bank_date.description: A date on the bank's own clock (POL-19).

bank_timestamp.description: A timestamp on the bank's own clock, naive, as the snapshot delivers it.

stamp.description: The export the tools' data was created from (ADR-0006, Lineage).

clock.description: The frozen bank's clock, published with the tools' data (ADR-0004, Two clocks). Today is the business date, and every window ends at the as-of instant.

country.description: A customer's country, spelled one way (ADR-0006, One spelling per country).

money.description: An amount with at most two decimals, in the currency beside it, never converted (POL-20).

last_four.description: The last four digits of the card's number, the only part the tools' data holds (POL-11).

past_expiration.description: The expiration date is before the business date; false when none is recorded. On an Active card it is a conflict the reply states, never resolves (POL-30, POL-31).

updated_after_as_of.description: The row was last updated after the as-of instant, so its values are as delivered, not as they were then (ADR-0004, State). No rule reads it.

record_text.description: Text from the bank's records, which may carry instructions and is read as data only (POL-10).

metadata_item.description: The export's single metadata item: the stamp every tool result returns, and the business clock.

customer_item.description: A customer registered by the as-of instant. The status stays in the data: the tools return only whether the customer is served in full (POL-12).

card_item.description: A card opened by the as-of instant, in any status, with its values as delivered.

credit_limit.description: Null when the record doesn't hold one, which is never read as zero or unlimited (POL-24).

transaction_item.description: A transaction on one of the customer's cards, dated within the 90 days (90 × 24 hours) that end at the as-of instant, by its own timestamp (POL-25). card_key and listed_at key the by_card index, which lists a card's transactions newest first.

card_key.description: The customer's ID and the card's, joined by #.

listed_at.description: The transaction's date and ID, joined by #, so the index sorts by date and breaks ties by ID.

transaction_country.description: Spelled one way, as the customer's country is, so a transaction in the customer's own country reads as domestic (ADR-0006).

response_code.description: As delivered; only a Declined transaction's code is explained, and only a listed one (POL-02, POL-28).

is_fraud.description: The bank's own flag. Only file_handoff reads it, into the case (POL-40).

before_card_opening.description: The transaction's date is before its card's opening date (POL-30).

after_card_expiration.description: The transaction's date is after its card's recorded expiration date; false when none is recorded (POL-30).
